LESSON: CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.8: Conversational Skills
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Conversational Skills, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 5 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can we take care of ourselves in different weather conditions? 2. How can we ensure etiquette when holding conversations?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to describe different weather patterns (e.g. sunny, rainy, windy, cold),

2. collaborate to play a language game

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to describe different weather patterns (e.g. sunny, rainy, windy, cold),
2. collaborate to play a language game

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Conversational Skills together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: This is promoted as the learner engages actively when playing a language game where

one uses non-verbal cues to describe a weather pattern and others try to guess which one it is.

• Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner engages in constructive dialogue when working jointly to describe different

weather patterns.

Values:
• Peace: This is promoted as the learner displays tolerance with peers when conducting singing games on various weather

patterns.

• Responsibility: This is promoted as the learner diligently engages in assigned roles when role playing a dialogue using turn

taking skills to describe the weather patterns.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental awareness: This is promoted as the learner appreciates the weather and interacts with content on weather and the

environment.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept about turn taking and conversational etiquette to their learning in English and Kiswahili.
